learningObjective: Distinguish nvcuda::wmma (C++ template API) from raw mma.sync PTX.

canonicalClaims.claim: nvcuda::wmma is a C++ template API providing fragment/load/store/mma primitives that compile down to `mma.sync` + `ldmatrix` PTX; raw PTX (used by CUTLASS and other libs) offers finer shape/layout control but both target the same hardware.
nonImplications: Does not imply wmma exposes every mma shape.
Does not imply raw PTX is always faster.

misconceptions.claim: wmma and mma.sync cannot be mixed.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They can coexist; wmma lowers to PTX at compile time.

misconceptions.claim: wmma is deprecated on Ampere and later.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It continues to be supported; lowering targets newer mma shapes.

misconceptions.claim: PTX mma.sync is unstable across CUDA versions.
misconceptions.whyWrong: PTX is a stable virtual ISA with documented versioning.

misconceptions.claim: wmma always outperforms raw PTX because the compiler knows optimal lowering.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Library-quality raw PTX can outperform wmma for niche shapes and layouts.

implementationFacts: wmma fragment shapes: m16n16k16 (fp16), m8n32k16, m32n8k16, etc.
CUTLASS uses raw PTX for maximum control (shape choice, register banking).
